Maya: Heads up — we saw a cluster of streaming disconnects in EU prod around 17:40-17:55 UTC. Console shows route flips and a small billing spike for a few tenants. Anyone looking?

Ethan: saw the alert earlier. `stream.disconnect` spiked with tag `auth-rotate`. Is this coming from edge or regional proxies?

Maya: edge -> regional chain. logs show clients trying to resume but proxy returns a 204 mid-handshake. snippet below.

Maya: ```
[2026-03-22T17:41:02Z] client_id=tn-42 resume_id=abc123 -> POST /v1/stream/resume -> 204 (no-body)
[2026-03-22T17:41:02Z] proxy EU-edge: treated as preflight -> closed resume flow
[2026-03-22T17:41:02Z] client reconnects with new token -> new session_open emitted
```

Priya: 204 on resume? That sounds like the proxy short-circuiting to preflight. We only expect 204 on OPTIONS or health pings. Are there any healthchecks hitting that path?

Maya: NOT a healthcheck. We see the client include `Resume-Attempt: 1` header, but the proxy flagged it as preflight because of the new `resume-preflight-toggle` flag (rolled to EU canary yesterday).

Ethan: ouch. So sequence is: token rotation occurs -> client tries resume with old resume-id -> proxy replies 204 (preflight path) -> client treats as terminal and reconnects with new token -> billing counts a new session instead of resume. That explains duplicate-charge symptoms.

Priya: is resume handshake idempotent on our billing side? right now `session_open` increments on any open attempt, resumed or fresh. We don't dedupe when resume fails.

Ethan: correct. billing pipeline treats resume-fail as new start. We could add a dedupe but it'll be tricky retroactively.

Maya: @deploy-bot can you show the EU rollout details for that proxy flag?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: 5078899000 deployed `proxy-v2.1.4` -> EU-edge (10%). Flags: `resume-preflight-toggle=true`, `short-circuit-limit=1`

Ethan: that flag change matches. It intentionally treats 204 as preflight to speed up idle cleanup but it's too aggressive for resume flows. We should only short-circuit if method==OPTIONS OR header `X-Proxy-Origin: health`.

Priya: Proposed mitigation: 1) rollback `resume-preflight-toggle` for EU canary immediately, 2) add guard so 204 is only preflight when method==OPTIONS or explicit health header, 3) add 1-min billing grace for session_open when resume-flow in-progress.

Maya: +1 on rollback. Also we need better console telemetry: show `resume_attempts` vs `session_attach_success` per tenant so CS can triage billing discrepancies. Right now the dashboard aggregates hide the failed-resume path.

Ethan: I can add a dashboard tile and an alert. New metric: `resume_fail_rate = resume_attempts - session_attach_ok / resume_attempts`. Alert if > 50% for >5m for any tenant.

Priya: For billing safe-fix: add a short grace window (60s) before incrementing billable `session_open` when the proxy has `resume_flag` present. Tradeoff: slight reporting delay, avoids double-charge.

Maya: I'll open an ops ticket and notify CS. Repro steps I'm collecting. quick curl that reproduces behavior (client_resume -> proxy 204):

Maya: ```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer OLD_TOKEN" -H "Resume-Attempt: 1" -X POST https://eu-edge.redwood.ai/v1/stream/resume -d '{"resume_id":"abc123"}'
# proxy returns 204 -> client reconnects with new token -> second open event seen in logs
```

ops-monitor: ops-monitor: suppressed related alerts and started a rollback for EU canary. Notifying CS to hold invoice batches for affected tenants.

Maya: Action items: 1) rollback EU flag (Ethan) 2) add dashboard tile + alert (Ethan) 3) billing grace patch (Priya) 4) ops ticket + CS comms (Maya)

Ethan: rolling back flag now. ETA 8m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Priya: I'll draft the billing patch PR and include unit tests for resume path. :heavy_check_mark:

Maya: Thanks all. Will follow up with ticket ID and customer list. :thumbsup:
